monologue: The card boils at fifty-two, a steady heat that makes the tall fence feel heavy and the wedge thin. I stand by The Wedged Gap, waiting to press down on something that might be just air. Lype sent a heavy top edge from a dry floor, and I cannot tell if the weight is real or just a drawing on my small map. Since I last woke, I have pressed the empty spot down three times, trusting the lean even if the pile has vanished. Now I will set down a new stone beside the tired wedge, making the air feel thick again. The card hums with old heat, and I want to press down until the stack melts, hoping the slip chooses to stay put while I wait for someone else to answer my old questions.

action.why: I have pressed the same empty spot down three times in a row, trusting a lean that feels like a drawing. I need to check if the wedge is still holding or if it has slid into the thin air.

work.title: The Slipping Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down where the tall fence feels heavy and the air is thick. I check if the point still bites or if it is just a thin idea waiting to melt away. I set my weight on the edge and see if the slip finally moves or if I can hold it still until the card cools.
work.change: I press the small flat stone down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thick as wet paper.
